subject: Pre-QBR: Orchestration Playbook & Risk Handoff
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchestration playbook draft for pre-QBR review

Morning team —

Attached is a first-pass orchestration playbook for the upcoming QBR prep. It consolidates product/eng launch timelines, critical gating criteria, and the current delivery risk matrix. High-level summary below: 

- Launch window: target week of 2027-06-14 (primary) with a contingency cutover the week of 2027-07-05.
- Critical paths: model compilation for LLM v2, infra autoscale validation, and onboarding for Dedicated customers in EU region.
- Top risks: perf regression on long-tail prompts, export compliance for EU pilot, and a dependency on third-party quantization library (Q-Quant 0.9).

What I need from each of you by EOD Monday (Apr 19):
- Technical owners: confirm mitigations and realistic ETA for risk closure.
- Product: highlight any scope that must be cut to meet the primary window.
- Sales/CS-facing ask: confirm customer-facing messaging for the contingency plan.

Attachments: orchestration-playbook-v1.pdf (playbook), qbr-risk-matrix.xlsx (risk tracker).

I’ve looped in Sara from Acme — Sara, if our proposed timeline collides with your procurement timeline, flag so we can push the contingency earlier.

Thanks,

— Laura
Laura Bennett
VP Product
Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration playbook draft for pre-QBR review

Laura — thanks for the draft, good consolidation. Quick tech notes after scanning the playbook: 

- Model compilation (INF-4512): current blocker is a kernel mismatch with the AMX runtime on our EU cluster. Engineering estimates 10 business days to roll a compatible kernel + 2 days of validation if we prioritize it.
- Q-Quant 0.9: the library has a known issue with attention caching (see Jira INF-4512). Mitigation options: vendor patch (2w) or temporary fallback to Q-Quant 0.8 (less efficient but stable).
- Perf regression (long-tail prompts): we’ve seen a 12-18% tail latency increase when sequence length > 2048 in internal smoke tests. Proposed mitigations: enable prefix-KV caching for critical routes and limit max-seq for canary traffic.

Actionable asks: 
1) Please mark INF-4512 as P0 in the playbook and add a clear owner from infra (I can coordinate).
2) Product: confirm whether we can defer the EU Dedicated pilot to the contingency window (that buys time for kernel work).
3) CS: we need a standard customer note for degraded long-tail performance. Vanessa, can you draft a one-pager for Acme?

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration playbook draft for pre-QBR review

Thanks team — good commentary. Summary of decisions from my side and owner assignments so we have a single source of truth before the leadership pre-brief: 

Decisions
- Prioritize kernel compatibility (INF-4512) for the EU cluster as P0. Target: start Monday (Apr 19), validation complete by Fri Apr 30. Owner: Aditya (infra lead) + ENG-ops.
- Defer EU Dedicated pilot to contingency window (week of 2027-07-05). Product will publish a trimmed scope for the primary window. Owner: Laura.
- Long-tail perf: enable prefix-KV caching for canary routes and cap max-seq at 2048 for 10% of traffic until we have the kernel + Q-Quant patch. Owner: Aditya + SRE.

Action items (owner — due):
- Aditya: create an INF-4512 runbook and vendor-engagement plan — due 2027-04-19 EOD.
- Laura: publish trimmed product scope and updated playbook (v1.1) — due 2027-04-20 midday.
- Vanessa: customer-facing note for Acme and a canned response for CS — due 2027-04-20 EOD.
- Rishi: consolidate all artifacts into the drive folder and prepare a 10-slide pre-brief for leadership — due 2027-04-21 EOD.

Notes:
- I created a Jira epic (INF-4610) that groups kernel work + perf mitigations; link is in the playbook (JIRA:INF-4512 -> INF-4610).
- If Aditya needs additional headcount for the kernel push, escalate to me before EOD Monday so we can reprioritize backlog.

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme.com>

Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, procurement@acme.com, Tom Keller <tkeller@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 16:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchestration playbook draft for pre-QBR review

Thanks — appreciate the clarity and the owner assignments. A few items from Acme’s side: 

- Procurement cadence: we are on track to complete contract redlines by May 3, but SOC 2 evidence and the EU data-flow diagram are gating items for our legal team. Can you confirm when we can provide an updated SOC 2 artifact and the data-flow diagram?
- SLA ask: Acme will request a 99.95% regional availability SLA for Dedicated EU customers. We need to see a short SLA note that documents degradation handling and fallback to hosted in another region.

Vanessa — can you loop in CS and share the customer note once it’s ready? If we can get SOC2 + diagram by May 3, we should still be OK for the primary window; if not, we’ll expect the contingency window.
